## Verdict

Dorado costs least for a team of 18, at $162 per month. It is the only vendor whose minimum (10 seats) falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly the seats it uses. Inkwell bills for 25 seats and Borealis for 50, so both charge for capacity the team will not touch.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $9 | 10 |
| Inkwell | $14 | 25 |
| Borealis | $19 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (18) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 10 is below 18, so 18 seats paid. 18 × $9 = **$162 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 25 exceeds 18, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $14 = **$350 per month**. Seven unused seats, worth $98.
- **Borealis:** minimum 50 exceeds 18, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $19 = **$950 per month**. Thirty-two unused seats, worth $608.

Dorado is $188 per month cheaper than Inkwell and $788 cheaper than Borealis — $2,256 and $9,456 over twelve months.

## Risks

Effective cost per working person tells the sharper story: Dorado $9.00, Inkwell $19.44 ($350 ÷ 18), Borealis $52.78 ($950 ÷ 18). Those penalties are artefacts of the minimums, not the rates.

Growth shifts the arithmetic but not the ranking. Inkwell's unused-seat penalty vanishes at 25 people, where it costs $350 against Dorado's $225; Borealis clears its floor only at 50. Dorado has the lowest per-seat rate on the list, so it stays cheapest at every headcount above 18.

This is a price comparison and nothing more. The list carries no detail on features, support, limits or contract terms, so the cheapest seat may not be a comparable product. Figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual terms or negotiated discounts are not covered here.
